name: Bronzer stick

card.summary: A cream bronzer in stick form swiped onto the cheekbones, temples and jawline to add warmth and shadow, so the face looks more sculpted.
card.note: Washes off; can rub onto clothing and look patchy if misapplied.

quick.overview:
A bronzer stick is a cream bronzer packaged like a deodorant stick or balm. It tints the skin a shade or two deeper and is used to add warmth or shadow along the cheekbones, hairline and jaw.

It helps looks temporarily: a darker line under the cheekbone or jaw can make the face seem more defined, and an all-over warm tone can make skin look healthier. The effect lasts until it is washed off.
quick.how: Users swipe the stick onto the areas they want to emphasise and blend with fingers or a sponge. Many reach for it for jaw and cheekbone contour. Results are immediate and fade with washing.
quick.risks: Bronzers tint the skin only until washed off [1]. Many contain fragrance or other allergens [1]. Rub-off on fabric and an orange or splotchy look can occur if misapplied [1].

lead: A bronzer stick is a cream bronzer in a twist-up or push-up stick. Bronzers in general are a temporary tint for the skin that lasts until washed off, similar to makeup, and they come as powders, sprays, mousses, gels, lotions and moisturizers [1].

In looksmaxxing and grooming circles the stick format is mentioned for contouring: a warm or slightly darker stripe along the cheekbone, temple or under the jawline to suggest shadow and structure. Sources on bronzers describe tanning and colour rather than contouring [1], so this use reflects how people apply the product.

chain: Stick applied along jaw and cheekbones
angle.text: The darker tint creates visible shadow where the user places it. The change shows right away and lasts until it is removed.

infobox: Walnut extract, jojoba extract, caramel (bronzers generally)

paras: Bronzers are not defined in law or by US FDA regulation, and common ingredients include walnut oil extract, jojoba extract and caramel [1]. Some also contain allergens such as benzyl alcohol, tocopherol and fragrance [1].
Most bronzers leave some rub-off where fabric meets skin, and misapplication can look orange or splotchy [1]. Cream formats are commonly applied directly from the stick and blended.
